blocking_findings.finding: The proposed `startedAtGenRef` boolean does not define a safe first-window/generation admission boundary. `ensureRendered` is asynchronous and reaches `doc.getPage()` before `page.render()` starts. If the flag changes only at actual `renderStart`, additional pages—including pages entering during fast scrolling—can concurrently observe `false` and bypass deferral. If it changes synchronously on the first invocation, only one page may bypass, contradicting the required immediate initial/zoom window. The plan also does not define how all active pages belonging to the exempt window are captured atomically.
blocking_findings.required_change: Replace the boolean-only rule with an explicit per-`(docId,genId)` admission epoch/batch. Define exactly when the exempt active-set snapshot is taken, admit every still-active mounted page in that snapshot, and close the exemption before later IO mutations can join it. Specify behavior across awaits and add deterministic tests proving: multiple initial pages render immediately, every active page after a generation commit is admitted, and pages entering afterward during continuous scrolling remain deferred.

blocking_findings.finding: Pending-admission ownership and race cleanup are incomplete. The plan clears pending work on document change/disposal but not explicitly on every `genId` change, although pending records contain only `(pageNumber, canvas)` and therefore carry no generation identity. A stale timer can consequently execute after a zoom/fit commit. The timer's call into the existing render path also lacks a specified gate-bypass/epoch token, canvas-identity check, and serialized revalidation, making recursive re-deferral, duplicate admission, stale-canvas rendering, or ceiling races possible.
blocking_findings.required_change: Specify pending entries with document/generation/admission-epoch and exact canvas identity; invalidate and clear the map and timer on every generation change, document change, and disposal. Timer callbacks must capture an epoch token, become no-ops when stale, remove/claim entries atomically, and immediately re-check disposed state, current doc/gen, active membership, mounted canvas identity, existing task/settle state, and the live-canvas ceiling before entering a clearly named ungated render-start path. Extend T3/T5/T6 to cover stale generation timers, disposal during expiry, canvas replacement, duplicate callbacks, and multiple final-window pages.

blocking_findings.finding: P-4a has been semantically weakened. The accepted contract measured each alternating 100%→200% or 200%→100% zoom commit from commit to settle. Sampling only the terminal 190%→200% step while leaving the preceding ten real commits unasserted is not equivalent to the user-visible 100%→200% operation, even though the terminal render uses the final scale. It removes nearly the entire forward traversal from the latency budget and makes the two directions asymmetric. Calling each step a separate product commit does not preserve the original alternating-target budget.
blocking_findings.required_change: Make an explicit product/contract decision instead of claiming equivalence. Either provide an approved real product gesture that commits directly from 100% to 200% and measure that gesture end-to-end, or amend P-4a transparently as a changed/weakened budget with appropriate design and acceptance review. If the intended requirement is user traversal latency through stepped controls, measure the complete 100%→200% traversal in the page clock, including every React commit and settle, with the unchanged 20-sample/19th≤500 ms threshold unless that threshold is formally reconsidered.

blocking_findings.finding: The P-4b repair places detection and replacement in one evaluation but does not require the initiating gesture to occur in that same evaluation. If the initial commit is issued through the driver first, the render can settle during the driver-to-page transition—the same class of race the repair is meant to remove. The plan also leaves gesture selection ambiguous at maximum zoom or when the requested fit mode is already active, so a dispatched click may be a disabled/no-op gesture rather than a real React-controlled generation commit.
blocking_findings.required_change: Define each overlap attempt as one in-page evaluation that resets/captures the baseline, dispatches one enabled real initiating control gesture, observes its new `genId` and unsettled `renderStart` by `seq`, then synchronously dispatches a distinct enabled replacement gesture and proves a second generation. Specify valid gesture pairs for every escalation rung, including max-zoom and current-fit-state cases, and fail the rung if either gesture does not produce the expected generation transition. Preserve the existing no-sleep, no-direct-state, full-stream, cancellation-ordering, and stale-paint assertions.

non_blocking_observations.observation: A 120 ms quiescence interval is reasonable for the exact 50 ms P-3 cadence because each genuine visible-set mutation re-arms it, and the 2 s terminal settle provides ample admission time. It should remain a production behavior constant rather than a harness-derived value; tests should cover cadence just below and pauses just above the boundary using fake timers.
